mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market, boosting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases by > 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) suggests increased consumer demand, which can lead to higher corporate revenues and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS increases by > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases by > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the instances when both UNRATE and PAYEMS meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST increases by > 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) coupled with a stable or increasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) suggests inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS remains stable or increases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the instances when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a contraction in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 decreases by > 0.5% within a quarter.
